interpretation: Descriptive run-level medians at 25 ms polling were lower for Solo: at 1000 ms configured scheduler/block cadence, client observation was 907 ms versus AFT 1481 ms and ordering/finalization was 48 ms versus 60 ms; at 100 ms cadence, client observation was 106 ms versus 1324 ms. Independent fresh chains produced different depth/version sample mixes, so these aggregates are not matched causal estimates and the 1000 ms/depth-matched buckets do not preserve the same ordering.

At 1000 ms configured scheduler/block cadence and 500 ms polling, client-observed p50 was effectively null at 1003 ms for Solo versus 1004 ms for AFT. All three AFT/Solo pairs are reported; per-transaction proposal wait and event-driven completion remain unmeasured.

Changing the poll interval produced values quantized near 500/1000/1500/2000/2500 ms. Independent fresh chains and differing version distributions prevent subtracting the poll runs into an exact notification cost.

No tested depth/version bucket shows the pre-repair seconds-to-minutes growth in ordering, state commitment or persistence. Solo reached version 4004 at depth 10 under 100 ms cadence without making IAVL commitment or Redb persistence the dominant phase.

The full semantic and restart parity, not an uncontrolled latency delta, supports treating single-authority/Solo as a deployment-profile candidate. It does not authorize deleting, weakening or demoting the AFT control or extrapolating to peer-bearing profiles.

explicit_nonclaims: No numeric latency tripwire is established.
No phase summary sums inclusive or nested values.
Proposal/cadence wait, admission/queueing and receipt creation/durable ACK are not separately measured.

Configured scheduler ticker and genesis block floor are not measured per-transaction proposal wait; realized proposal spacing was unavailable because no attributed adjacent-height pair qualified for differencing.
Event-driven completion latency is not measured.
Independent fresh chains produced different depth/version mixes, so cross-profile aggregate latency differences are descriptive and not matched causal estimates.
The single-validator fixture exercises no cross-node ordering and says nothing about either engine with peers.
No profile transition or dual-authority interval was exercised; each fresh run selected one profile before start.
No proof generation, proof size or cryptographic proof verification is measured.
Signed heads or finality certificates alone do not establish non-equivocation, freshness, revocation status, admission correctness or present authority.
The pre-repair quadratic canonical-collapse behavior was a usage defect, not an inherent BFT cost.
ReceiptCheckpoint v1 remains the linear ioi.receipt-hash-chain-jcs-sha256.v1 contract.
The proposed portable-proof successor is not the already-implemented M03.5 portable v3 authority grant verifier and is not implemented here.
M04.6 ownership, the one-spine law, the deterministic blocking lane and the scheduled release-qualification soak are unchanged.
